                            North Central Texas Council of Governments




       NORTH CENTRAL TEXAS COUNCIL OF GOVERNMENTS EXECUTIVE SUMMARY

The North Central Texas Council of Governments (NCTCOG) appreciates the efforts of
Commission Staff to develop a standard for large load interconnection to balance minimization
of stranded infrastructure, ensure reliability, and support business development. The following
comments are presented for consideration in refining draft 16 TAC §25.194 and in future efforts
on large loads.

   •    NCTCOG recommends Commission Staff consider collaboration with other state
        agencies to ensure this draft rule does not create unintended consequences such as
        increased noise and air pollution.

   •    NCTOG recommends making available information on the total deployment of back-up
        generation systems at LLEs.

The North Central Texas Council of Governments (NCTCOG) is a voluntary association of, by and for
local governments, established to assist in regional planning in 16-counties in North Central Texas.
NCTCOG respectfully submits these comments, responding to Commission Staff's December 2,
2025, memorandum requesting input on draft 16 TAC §25.194 Large Load Interconnection
Standards.

    1. GENERAL COMMENTS ON DRAFT 16 TAC §24.194

NCTCOG supports Commission Staffs draft 16 TAC §25.194 and appreciates the focus on reducing
the risk of stranded infrastructure, supporting business development, and ensuring grid reliability.
NCTCOG respectfully offers the following observations.

The Electric Reliability Council of Texas (ERCOT) operational standards, as presented in §25.194(I),
provide an authority to create standards for Large Load Entities (LLEs) to curtail load or to deploy
backup generation, if available, at LLEs during times of high grid demand. In the aggregate,
deployment of backup generation systems may have unintended economic and environmental
impacts for the region in which they are deployed. For example, the sudden deployment of many
natural gas and/or diesel generators could cause significant noise and air pollution, which can
negatively impact the quality of life of surrounding communities. Therefore, it is recommended that
Commission Staff consider collaboration with other state regulatory agencies to explore potential
unintended consequences from deployment of backup generation systems.

   •   In the event of an Energy Emergency Alert from ERCOT and the deployment of backup
        generation systems, there is no mechanism for entities to obtain operational information
       concerning the backup generation systems deployed, such as the fuel type(s) of generations
       or length of deployment. NCTCOG recommends Commission Staff consider provisions for
       ERCOT to maintain and to make available to the public data at the county level on the
       generation capacity, total number of backup generation systems available, total number of

    2. CLOSING

NCTCOG appreciates the Commission Staff's diligent work on draft 16 TAC §25.194, and the
opportunity to provide input on Project No. 58481. NCTCOG respectfully registers these
recommendations with Commission Staff for consideration in refining draft 16 TAC §25.194 and
in future efforts on large loads.
